listings.content: Inspired by the Weißenhofsiedlung in Stuttgart and initiated by architect Josef Frank, the Werkbundsiedlung public estate housing project in the Lainz Municipality of Hietzing was built from 1930 to 1932 by numerous national and international architects of the time (amongst those famous names like Adolf Loos and Gerrit Rietvelt) and has fine examples of Bauhaus style architecture. This public estate housing complex consisted of 76 buildings of which 32 still exist.
listings.image: Andre Lurcat, 1931-1932, A1130 Wien, Veitingergasse 87-93, Werkbundsieldung.jpg

listings.name: Hietzinger Cemetery
listings.content: Many prominent Viennese from the 18th to the 20th centuries are buried here, including the playwright Franz Grillparzer, painter Gustav Klimt, architect Otto Wagner, and modern composer Alban Berg.

listings.name: Klimt Villa
listings.content: The painter Gustav Klimt used this villa as a studio from 1911 until his death in 1918. The studio has been carefully reconstructed using old photographs, and other rooms in the villa have displays about Klimt's models and clients.

listings.name: Hietzinger Pfarrkirche
listings.content: Dating back to the 15th century, the church was destroyed in the Turkish war of 1685 and was rebuilt in the Baroque style.

listings.name: Lainzer Tiergarten
listings.content: A beautiful nature reserve which was once the Emperor's private hunting wood; on the grounds is the Hermesvilla, the favorite mansion of Empress Elisabeth. It has several 2-10 km hiking trails. Local recreation area, in summer you can see wild pigs, deer, and many Viennese families.

listings.name: Hietzinger Bad
listings.content: There is both an indoor and outdoor pool.

listings.name: Bikepath Vienna river
listings.content: A short ride of 7km is available without any traffic crossings.

listings.name: Gasthaus Lindwurm
listings.content: The place has retro charm. There is a nearby playground for kids, hence it is a very family-friendly Austrian restaurant. The place directly borders the Viennese woods.

listings.name: Kichererbse
listings.content: The shop has a changing daily lunch vegan plate, salads and soup.

listings.name: Napoleonwald
listings.content: The restaurant specialises in fresh fish. It is also very kid-friendly.

listings.name: Hermes Café Restaurant Labstelle
listings.content: The restaurant is non-smoking and serves breakfast till 11:30.

listings.name: Café Dommayer
listings.content: Nonsmoking, without outdoor seating.

listings.name: Cafe Gloriette
listings.content: Inside the Gloriette with good view over to the Schönbrunn palace serves early breakfast, café and cakes. One has to climb up the hill of the Schönbrunn park to reach it.

listings.name: Café am Platz
listings.content: It serves all day breakfast

listings.name: Landtmann’s Jausen Station
listings.content: The renovated Meierei serves good breakfast between 09:00-14:00 in this beautiful location.

listings.name: Heurigenschenke Zur Wildsau
listings.content: The Heurigen has a big garden with a good view over Vienna.

listings.name: Schneider-Gössl
listings.content: The oldest Heurigen in the Ober St. Veit part of Hietzing.

listings.name: Hostel Hütteldorf
listings.content: This Youth Hostel is preferred by students.

listings.name: Schneider Gössl
listings.content: The hotel also rents apartments.

listings.name: Parkhotel Schönbrunn
listings.content: The hotel is in front of the Schönbrunn park. Guests of Emperor Franz Joseph used to reside here when they had to wait for an audience.

listings.name: Haydnhaus
listings.content: Joseph Haydn spent the final twelve years of his life in this home, during which time he composed the oratorios The Creation and The Seasons. The house has been a museum since 1899, and careful restoration has included the small garden, which is now also open to the public.
listings.price: €4 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/Vienna Card), free (children/youth under 19), free the first Sunday of every month

listings.name: Haus des Meeres
listings.content: A marvelous zoo, with a rain forest glasshouse, tiny apes, aquariums with sharks, and terrariums with reptiles and venomous snakes. Other highlights include an interesting exhibit of Mediterranean sea life and the aquarium's beloved sea turtle, "Puppi." The apes and birds are allowed to freely mingle with the visitors, but don't attempt to touch or feed them. It is in one of the surviving air raid defense towers from WWII, a so-called Flakturm. During wartime, the building provided fire control for Vienna's anti-aircraft artillery, housed some of the first radar equipment, and is designed to withstand a direct bomb hit, an earthquake, and wind speeds up to an overpressure of ten bar. Its former gun emplacements are now a platform on top affording nice views over the roofs of Vienna.

listings.name: Rahlstiege
listings.content: The staircase connects the Mariahilfer and the Gumpendorfer Strasse. It was built in 1870.

listings.name: Kletterzentrum Flakturm
listings.content: On one side of the 2nd Worldwar bunker there are routes to climb high up until its roof with great views into the roofs of Vienna. The routes are usually hard and require some endurance. The alpine club organises courses for beginners and intermediate. On the other side there are boulder problems set. The outdoor climbing in middle of a historic city makes this a favorite choice for many climbers during the hot season.

listings.name: Theater an der Wien
listings.content: This historic theater was founded by Emanuel Schikaneder (best known as Mozart's librettist for The Magic Flute). The building was designed by Franz Jäger, and completed in 1801. Since opening it has been the venue for many historic premieres of opera, theatre, and symphonies, including Beethoven's Fidelio in 1805 and Johann Strauss II's Die Fledermaus in 1874; since 2006 it has functioned mostly as an opera house. The side entrance, known as Papagenotor, has a sculpture of Papageno, the character whose role was Schikaneder played in the premiere of The Magic Flute.

listings.name: Raimund Theater
listings.content: Constructed in 1893 as a venue for German folk dramas and plays, the building was later used for operettas. Since 1985 it has hosted German-language and international musicals.

listings.name: Apollo Kino
listings.content: A Cineplexx theater with plenty of choices including original versions. The cinema opened here in 1905. According to seat numbers it is one of the biggest in Vienna.

listings.name: Haydn Kino
listings.content: The theatre projects mostly English films in original version.

listings.name: Topkino
listings.content: During football championships they show the games in one of the cinema theatres. It is screening international artistic productions. For the bar see the drink section.

listings.name: Café Do An
listings.content: Several salads are served. Free Wi-Fi. Usually it is well packed by a "bobo" public.

listings.name: Eis-Greissler
listings.content: Serves vegan and interesting ice-cream varieties.

listings.name: Natsu I
listings.content: Decent sushi.

listings.name: Cafe Willendorf
listings.content: The restaurant inside the lesbian and queer "Rosa Lilla Villa" serves good international food.

listings.name: Disco Volante
listings.content: Pizza with just enough and not too many toppings, and very Italian selection. Austrian ingredients, when used, are unusual specialties.

listings.name: Kuishimbo
listings.content: The smallest Japanese restaurant in town. All the dishes are homemade, and the owners claim that they pay attention to a proper balance of ingredients – being full can also be healthy. The place is so small that there is no toilet inside, you have to use the one in the Naschmarkt. The udon soups are excellent.

listings.name: Mythos
listings.content: A nice family-run Greek restaurant, with a good variety of items to choose from.

listings.name: Naschmarkt Deli
listings.content: Popular student meet place in Naschmarkt that sells directly sells good food with many vegetarian options directly from the Naschmarkt. The Italian café is recommended. Later in the evenings often a DJ plays.

listings.name: Salzberg
listings.content: The Salzberg restaurant serves Pongauer Kasnocken, made with special smoked cheese (Räucherkäse) from Salzburg province. There is a large selection of breakfast/brunch choices. The open air patio is on a quiet street.

listings.name: Schwarze Katze
listings.content: Georges Dimou, the singer, operates this traditional Greek restaurant.

listings.name: Fischrestaurant Umar
listings.content: Extremely good fish directly from their shop, which is the best and freshest seafood shop in Vienna. Wi-Fi is available. Changing daily lunch menu.

listings.name: Neni
listings.content: The best restaurant on the Naschmarkt with Isrealean carte.

listings.name: Café Drechsler
listings.content: The café is open during nights. It opened in 1919 by Engelbert Drechsler and is a traditional and popular all-night meeting point. It was carefully remodeled in 2007.

listings.name: Cafe Jelinek
listings.content: Small coffee place nicely lost in the middle of Mariahilf. In winter the rustic and warm oven is wonderful. In summer one can sit outdoors.

listings.name: Cafe Restaurant Gschamster Diener
listings.content: Smaller congenial Viennese café.

listings.name: Café Ritter
listings.content: A traditional Viennese cafe that is very popular due to its central location on Mariahilfer Strasse.

listings.name: Café Savoy
listings.content: The queer bar is centered around a big mirror and decorated in Makart style (Makartstil). Free WiFi. The café serves breakfast.

listings.name: Café Sperl
listings.content: A very traditional Viennese café, known to be frequented by contemporary Austrian writers including R. Menasse. It offers breakfast, cakes and a great atmosphere. Don't be put off by the Viennese brusqueness of the waiters – if possible counter with Viennese dialect and humor.

listings.name: Phil
listings.content: The bar/café sells also books, LPs and its furniture. The Pellini-Espresso is served from a Faema machine. Nice place to have breakfast.

listings.name: Topkino
listings.content: The bar of the cinema has good food too and serves wine and beer in a relaxed atmosphere. Unfortunately only up to 22:00 the bar is non-smoking, soon before people start smoking.

listings.name: Barfly's Club
listings.content: Big selection of fine and rare bottles.

listings.name: Bar Italia
listings.content: The Italian styled bar offers many different cocktails. Free Wi-Fi access. The music is primarily jazz and there is a dance floor.

listings.name: futuregarden
listings.content: Tiny little artsy bar, smoking permitted.

listings.name: If dogs run free
listings.content: The stylish and hip bar serves interesting cocktails.

listings.name: Joanelli
listings.content: The bar permits smoking and offers wines and vegan snacks.

listings.name: Tanzcafé Jenseits
listings.content: The bar serves good wine, with a popular dance floor (unusual in Vienna). Well-liked by women.

listings.name: Red Carpet Hostel
listings.content: Free WiFi, hostel bar, free welcome drink, shower/toilet in every room, backyard, free luggage storage. 1 Jul-14 Sep.

listings.name: Hotel Kummer
listings.content: Directly located on Mariahilferstraße.

listings.name: Hotel Fuerst Metternich
listings.content: The hotel is near Mariahilferstrasse and offers large breakfast. It hosts the Barfly's Club.

listings.name: Das Tyrol
listings.content: A small and comfortable hotel.

listings.name: Leopold Museum
listings.content: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside.
listings.price: €12, students €8, children apprentice, disabled €7, €1 per person for the cloak room service

listings.name: MUMOK
listings.content: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside. Has a self-service locker.

listings.name: Kunsthalle Wien
listings.content: Hosts highly-regarded exhibits of contemporary art, from Austrian and international artists.

listings.name: WestLicht Center for Photography
listings.content: Has a permanent exhibit of unusual cameras, including underwater and toy cameras, KGB spy cameras, and one of the 30 modified Hasselblad cameras used on the Apollo moon mission. The gallery hosts temporary exhibits, and the renowned "World Press Photo" show for the world's best press pictures.

listings.name: Möbel Museum Wien
listings.content: Houses the largest furniture collection in the world. The exhibit displays furniture for all the Austrian emperors since Charles VI (the father of Maria Theresa), furniture by the Thonet Brothers, Jugendstil, and the Viennese Modernist movement. In addition, they show other contemporary Austrian architects and designers, such as E.A. Plischke, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky, Luigi Blau, and Franz West. Besides the permanent furniture collection, the museum also hosts two to three temporary exhibitions on furniture design and photography each year. You can purchase a single ticket or a Sisi Ticket, which allows you entrance to the Schönbrunn Palace, the Imperial Apartments, Sisi Museum, and the Imperial Silver Collection in the Hofburg. Wheelchair-accessible.

listings.name: Volkstheater Vienna
listings.content: Designed by Hermann Helmer and Ferdinand Fellner, the theatre was built in 1889. With 970 seats it is the largest theatre in Vienna (larger than even the Burgtheater) and is one of the largest German-language theatres. It is located next to the Museumsquartier.

listings.name: Theater Am Spittelberg
listings.content: Historically one of the Pawlatschentheater, it has been renovated and is a venue for concerts and comedies.

listings.name: Filmhaus am Spittelberg
listings.content: With a single hall, this small and modern theatre screens documentary and arthouse films. Reservations are recommended.

listings.name: Bellaria Kino
listings.content: Charming and beautiful old-school cinema screening both old classic and original versions of contemporary films.

listings.name: Bortolotti
listings.content: An ice cream parlour worth visiting. Ask particularly for the Campari-Orange ice cream or try some other exotic flavors.
listings.address: Mariahilfer Straße 22 and 94 (the latter closed during winter!)

listings.name: Kolar Zieglergassemore
listings.content: Nice pubs/beisls. They have a tasty Fladenbrot as well as their own beer.

listings.name: Maschu
listings.content: A trendy hang out place with its own unique vibe, in the area of the city frequented by art students. It is famous for its falafel.

listings.name: Natsu II
listings.content: Serves decent sushi.

listings.name: Schnitzelwirt Schmidt
listings.content: The traditional Viennese food is excellent and served in truly prodigious portions. The Bauernschmaus (Farmer's Feast), a nearly incapacitatingly large schnitzel plate, which in combination with any of the wonderful on-tap beers, may necessitate an afternoon nap.

listings.name: Amerlingbeisl
listings.content: The restaurant has a good selection of food with vegetarian options too. Inside smoking is permitted, but this is not so much of a problem for non-smokers in summer when it's possible to sit outside. The bar serves beer, some wines, and standard cocktails.

listings.name: Bombay
listings.content: It serves the best Bombay Gin in Vienna. Among Indian restaurants in Vienna it is an institution, offering good food and large servings for reasonable prices.

listings.name: DschungelCafe
listings.content: A very child-friendly cafe and restaurant, located in the same building as the DschungelWien.at children's theater.

listings.name: Gasthaus Grünauer
listings.content: A Viennese restaurant serving high-quality food with a good selection of wines.

listings.name: MQdaily
listings.content: Located next to the entry of the MQ, this place is quite small and packed.

listings.name: I Ragazzi
listings.content: This Italian restaurant has good pizzas and pastas for good prices. Their fish soup is highly recommended. Outdoor seating is available in the summer.

listings.name: I Terroni
listings.content: Same crew as I Ragazzi but less crowded. The restaurant serves good Italian pizzas and pastas.

listings.name: Tian Bistro am Spittelberg
listings.content: Operated by star chef Paul Ivić of TIAN Restaurant, the bistro serves more affordable meals than at his main restaurant, all of them vegetarian with many vegan options. Reservations can be made online.

listings.name: Le Troquet
listings.content: A popular French bistro in a shabby chic setting. They play jazz and serve good wines; smoking permitted.

listings.name: Ulrich
listings.content: In a calm paved passage the small restaurant (Beisl) serves a breakfast and has a lunch menu.

listings.name: LUX Restaurant
listings.content: One part of the establishment is a café, and the other a bar and restaurant (by the Spittelberggase entrance). The food is regional and exquisite. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Veganista
listings.content: Operated by two vegan sisters, this is the first vegan ice cream shop in Vienna. It has become so popular that they have now expanded with four more branches in the Vienna area. Flavours change by season, many of them exotic.

listings.name: Blue Box
listings.content: This longstanding bar was legendary during the 1980s and 90s. It serves breakfast with many vegetarian options, as well as special beer from Vorarlberg.

listings.name: Café Leopold
listings.content: A classy modern café that becomes a bar in the evening. There may be a cover charge for the evening parties downstairs.

listings.name: Cafe Nil
listings.content: This Middle Eastern cafe is modeled after old coffee houses in Cairo and Alexandria, and serves many organic foods. Takeaway is available, although the atmosphere really invites one to linger.

listings.name: Café Westend
listings.content: Opened in 1900, the café has historic decor with old tables and mirrors. It is situated in front of the main railway station Westbahnhof, which makes it practical to wait here for upcoming trains.

listings.name: Das Möbel
listings.content: Hip café. Take a close look at the tables, chairs, and lamps – every piece of furniture is unique and for sale.

listings.name: Espresso
listings.content: Very cool little 1950s-style café with good tunes, attracting an eclectic crowd. Owned by the nearby Wirr bar.

listings.name: Europa
listings.content: The café is often bursting at the seams, but good tunes and decent service prevail. Good people watching and decor. One of Vienna's most popular meeting points. The bar serves warm food til late hours.

listings.name: TartaTata
listings.content: This small café serves French croissants, pains au chocolat, and tartes.

listings.name: Rote Bar
listings.content: Lovely interior to savour a relaxed drink inside the Volkstheater. From time to time it serves as a small venue for excellent concerts. The door is on the left side of the main entrance for the Volkstheater.

listings.name: Siebensternbräu
listings.content: An excellent Biergarten. They serve their own brews, which are all excellent. There is the usual assortment of bar food, friendly staff, and outdoor seating underneath an old linden tree in the middle of a hidden courtyard. Everyday from 11:00-16:00 a selection of hearty dishes is served for €5-6. Move indoors well before 23:00, because a local noise ordinance requires the bar to shut down the patio and the interior tables fill up quickly.

listings.name: Youth Hostel Vienna-Myrthengasse
listings.content: Institutional.

listings.name: K+K Maria Theresia
listings.content: Offers a gourmet breakfast buffet. Overall, this is a good choice both for a business traveler and for a family with a toddler; comfortable for non-smokers. Heated floors in bathroom. Rooms are modern and each has a full tea set, wired internet in every room, electronic safe box, hairdrier, minibar. Small sauna adjoining a tiny gym open until at least 23:00. Breakfast from 06:30. On the downside, few steps to overcome to get to the hotel with a stroller.
listings.price: Regular doubles around €125 through frequently available special offers, €145+ as rack rates

listings.name: Falkensteiner Hotel am Schottenfeld
listings.content: The hotel's contemporary design is a refreshing departure from the usually stodgy appearance of most Viennesse hotels. Be mindful when booking a suite – some of them come with steeply sloping roofs.

listings.name: Arcotel Wimberger Wien
listings.content: A surprisingly ordinary hotel from a chain priding itself in adding a designer touch to its properties. What matters, however, is that the (quite awfully decorated) rooms close to the Westbahnhof can be had for a reasonable price, and the service level is good for Vienna.

listings.name: InterCityHotel Wien
listings.content: The InterCityHotel chain, a part of the German Steigenberger Group, focuses on hotels right next to train stations. This particular one is a block away from Westbahnhof, but still offers all the usual amenities, including a free all-day ticket for public transit. The decor is simple but modern and tasteful, especially for Viennesse standards. Some more expensive Business Plus rooms feature terraces with a view over the rooftops of Vienna.

listings.name: NH Wien City
listings.content: NH brings the peace of mind by offering predictability of the chain's usual standards. Of note is the generous size of rooms (25m²), unusual for Vienna, as well as the fact that all of them are equipped with a kitchenette.

listings.name: NH Collection Wien Zentrum
listings.content: If the large rooms of the NH Wien City are still not enough for you, the chain's other property down the road offers suites of 35-50m² at similar prices.

listings.name: 25hours Hotel beim MuseumsQuartier
listings.content: The Viennese foothold of the outlandish designer hotel chain spanning the German-speaking countries, with a rooftop terrace bar so popular that even staying guests may find it hard to get in. The location between university campuses and the Museumsquartier helps enhance the artsy/cultural/intellectual setting.

listings.name: Hotel Sans Souci
listings.content: Opened in December 2012, Hotel Sans Souci Wien is right across from the Museum Quarter and a 5-minute walk from the Ringstraße. The large spa area includes an indoor pool. Free Wi-Fi is available.

listings.name: Liechtenstein Museum
listings.content: A private collection of the Prince of Liechtenstein is exhibited in his former Viennese residences, which include the Stadtpalais (City Palace) and Gartenpalais (Garden Palace). The richly decorated picture gallery mainly exhibits Baroque paintings, with a nice portion of Rubens. Guided tours on selected Fridays in German only, registration required.
listings.price: €25 (Stadtpalais), €20 (Gartenpalais); €38 (single ticket for both palaces); no discounts

listings.name: Pathologisch-anatomisches Bundesmuseum
listings.content: Housed in a squat tower, which once was an insane asylum, the Narrenturm (Fool's Tower), this museum contains some of the dustier corners of the annals of medicine. You will find preserved hydrocephalic infants, wax castings of tertiary syphilis, antique medical devices, and even a laryngeal tuberculous ulcer. The gift shop sells postcards depicting the best of these.

listings.name: Josephinum
listings.content: Founded by Emperor Joseph II as the Academy of Medico-Surgery, the building was completed in 1785 and houses nearly 1200 anatomical wax models commissioned by the emperor, along with medical documents and instruments. The Josephinum is still used for research today.

listings.name: Votivkirche
listings.content: One of the most important Neo-Gothic religious architectural sites in the world, constructed between 1856 and 1879. Stands on a large square on the location where an unsuccessful attempt to assassinate Emperor Franz Joseph took place in 1853. The plans were established by Heinrich von Ferstel (1828-1883), who chose to build the cathedral, borrowing heavily from the architecture of Gothic French cathedrals. It is made of white sandstone, similar to the Stephansdom, which is very vulnerable to air pollution and acid rain and therefore requires frequent renovations.

listings.name: Spittelau Waste Incineration Plant
listings.content: A waste incinerator may not be the usual item to attract a visitor's attention, but after the Viennese painter/architect Friedensreich Hundertwasser restyled the plant's façade in 1989 (following a fire in 1987), it has become a surprisingly photogenic fixture in the cityscape. Guided tours December 2020 are offered (in German only) for visitors wanting to gain more insight into Vienna's waste, recycling, and disposal systems; however it is possible to appreciate the exterior of the plant from many locations in the city.

listings.name: Strudlhofstiege
listings.content: Designed by Theodor Johann Jaeger and completed in 1910, the outdoor staircase connects Strudlhofgasse and Liechtensteinstraße, and is a significant example of Jugendstil architecture.

listings.name: St. Johannes Nepomuk Kapelle
listings.content: Designed by Otto Wagner between 1893 bis 1897, this is the architect's first religious structure and served as a model for his later Kirche am Steinhof.
listings.image: Johann-Nepomuk-Kapelle "St Joanni" - erster Sakralbau von Otto Wagner in Wien.jpg

listings.name: Freud Museum
listings.content: This small museum is in Freud's historic flat where he practiced psychoanalysis for almost his whole life. However, the collection is limited mostly to documents of various kinds relating to Freud's life. Almost all of the flat's contents, including the famous original couch, went along with Freud to London when he fled the Nazis in 1939 and are now in the Freud Museum there.

listings.name: Schubert Geburtshaus
listings.content: Franz Schubert was born in a small apartment in this house in 1797. The museum, just like the apartment itself, is rather small and not wheelchair accessible. The top floor displays documents relating to the composer's life and work, while other rooms display paintings by the Austrian writer Adalbert Stifter.
listings.price: €5 (adults), €4 (seniors/students/Vienna Card), free (children and youth under 19), free the first Su of every month

listings.name: Jüdischer Friedhof Seegasse
listings.content: Vienna's oldest preserved Jewish cemetery, in use from the 16th century until 1784. In 1941 Nazi officials decided to raze the cemetery; in response a number of Viennese Jews removed 931 gravestones and buried them at the Zentralfriedhof. In the 1980s 280 of the gravestones were rediscovered and returned to their original locations. The cemetery was resanctified in 1984. Due to ongoing restoration work (as of late 2016) the cemetery cannot be entered, but can be easily viewed from an elevated walkway overlooking the site.

listings.name: Volksoper
listings.content: The "People's Opera" is a venue for operettas, classical musicals, and ballet productions, as well as lighter traditional operas. Italian operas are often sung in German, and operas occasionally have English subtitles. Attendees under 15 receive a 75% discount.

listings.name: Schauspielhaus
listings.content: A small theatre.

listings.name: WUK
listings.content: WUK is a 12,000-m² space of culture, workshops, and social gathering. The cultural center regularly hosts concerts. The place was occupied by squatters in the early 1970s; these days it offers room for different cultural initiatives including rehearsal rooms, photographer black rooms, and a bike repair center.

listings.name: Votiv Kino
listings.content: The cinema screens international movies including many French ones. The annual Vienna Film Festival is hosted here. On Sunday morning there is a film breakfast. The cinema opened in 1912.

listings.name: Pier9
listings.content: The outdoor lead wall is 21.5 m high. There are 6 security lines with 13 routes. The boulder wall is downstairs next to the stream and has the same texture concrete wall with different inclinations.

listings.name: Gasthaus Wickerl
listings.content: Traditional Austrian tavern from an excellent kitchen.

listings.name: Statt-Beisl
listings.content: The student tavern inside of the WUK offers international food and several vegetarian offers.

listings.name: The Highlander
listings.content: Offers own beer and a nice variety of dishes, including vegetarian dishes, at a small square. Might not be one of the cheapest in the cheap section, but definitely worth the price.

listings.name: Wiener Deewan
listings.content: Young, urban Pakistani restaurant. All you can eat, pay as you wish. You can mix your own menu from a variety of curries, meat, rice, salads, and sauces. Vegetarians will have good choices.

listings.name: Zuppa
listings.content: Nice buffet and good choice of soups including some vegan options. Take-away.

listings.name: Lane & Merriman’s
listings.content: The Irish pub not only serves Irish food together with a big beer and whiskey choice it also sells bread (Blaa Bread, Treacle Bread) and apples.

listings.name: Pizza Riva
listings.content: Pizza Napoletana with good flavour.

listings.name: Rebhuhn
listings.content: A classic Viennese restaurant with daily changing menu with traditional meat food plus a great choice of Knödel.

listings.name: Stomach
listings.content: The restaurant serves contemporary Austrian cuisine, with many Styrian influences. It is highly rated and very popular. Reservations are recommended.

listings.name: Zum roten Bären
listings.content: The restaurant serves Austrian food classics combined with Slovenian food with great quality cooked by Hans Bodingbauer. It has Černá-Hora beer and interesting white wines per glass sold cheaply.

listings.name: Flein
listings.content: On the French ground of the French culture institute this restaurant serves good food. The lunch menu consists of two choices with one being vegetarian. Dogs are not allowed. In the nice season one can enjoy the garden. The wine selection is good and the Austrian beer is from Schrems.

listings.name: Good Morning Vietnam
listings.content: Vietnamese authentic restaurant serving refined food.

listings.name: Charlie P's Pub and Dining Room
listings.content: The Irish pub is very popular. It sells of course Irish beer, and fish and chips. It has a wide non-smoking area.

listings.name: Halbestadt
listings.content: The cocktail bar fills quickly, hence it is considered wise to reserve places. The cocktails are done with lots of knowledge and excellent alcohols. Consider asking for their specials as they give good advice. The barkeeper participates to international contests. The card designed by the owner and barkeeper Erich Wassicek varies along season. They serve many classics.

listings.name: Stiegl Ambulanz
listings.content: A good bar run by the Stiegl brewery where you can enjoy their beer, which is one of Austria's best common beers. The bar is popular for students with its modern furnishings and relaxed atmosphere. Try the Paracelsus, which you only get in Stiegl breweries.

listings.name: The Sign
listings.content: This lounge bar serves experimental cocktails by trained keepers. The cocktails are very laboriously mixed. Very friendly service. From the outside the bar is almost not noticeable, but elongates towards the interior. The card offers many creative choices plus one gets ask for interesting local advices by the waiter. Cocktails marked with the asterisk are served in special bowls during the week.

listings.name: Weinstadt
listings.content: Every Wednesday the wine bar organises a specific wine tasting. One can choose between many Austrian or international wines.

listings.name: Universitats Brauhaus
listings.content: Charming beer garden in the Altes AKH campus of the University of Vienna. They serve traditional Viennese pub food as well as excellent BBQ ribs.

listings.name: Café Stein
listings.content: A café that is a popular students' meeting point. It has modern stylish interior.

listings.name: Café Francais
listings.content: The brasserie offers a simple French bistro food choice.

listings.name: Café Weimar
listings.content: A traditional Viennese café where one can listen every day after 19:30 to piano music.

listings.name: Weltcafé
listings.content: The café serves fairtrade food and café. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Hotel Pension Liechtenstein
listings.content: The family establishment is near the centre.

listings.name: Hotel Goldener Baer
listings.content: This is a modest hotel. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Pension Ani Falstaff
listings.content: The family-run bed and breakfast is centrally located.
listings.price: Low season: singles €50-56, doubles €76-78; peak season: singles €62-68, doubles €86-94

listings.name: Hotel & Palais Strudlhof
listings.content: Next to the famous stairs "Strudlhof".

listings.name: Palais Auersperg
listings.content: The palace was built in the early 18th century, and expanded in the late 18th century under the ownership of Prince Adam von Auersperg. Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach drew up the first plans; later designs are attributed to Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt. In 1945 the Austrian resistance group O5 (meaning OE = Oesterreich) met here. Historically it has always been a center for music, hosting many celebrations and balls. Today various events are organised here.

listings.name: Palais Damian
listings.content: The palace changed hands frequently, with each owner making their own adaptations to the building. The central sections date from the early 18th century, while the second floor was a later addition.

listings.name: Palais Schönborn
listings.content: This impressive Baroque palace was built in 1706-1711 following the designs of Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt. It houses the Museum of Folk Life and Folk Art (Museum für Volkskunde) (see listing below).

listings.name: Palais Strozzi
listings.content: The palace was built in 1702, and once had a garden that extended to Pfeilgasse. Renovations in 1996 led to the rediscovery of old paintings dating to the period of the building's construction.

listings.name: Piarist Church
listings.content: The Baroque church Maria Treu was probably designed by Lukas von Hildebrandt. The church has eight chapels and is decorated with frescoes made by Franz Anton Maulbertsch. It is considered as an important religious building of its time. In 1949 it was elevated to Basilica minor.

listings.name: Wiener Schuhmuseum
listings.content: The only museum of its kind in Austria, with displays focusing on the history of shoemaking.

listings.name: Österreichisches Museum für Volkskunde
listings.content: Founded in 1895 and housed in the Schönborn Garden Palace, this museum is dedicated to preserving the traditional folk art of Austria and of central Europe, with rotating exhibits as well as a permanent display. There is a museum library and gift shop onsite, and guided tours are available in German, English, and Slovak.

listings.name: Kletterzentrum ÖGV
listings.content: A small climbing gym inside Vienna has walls in an indoor court, in the cellar, and more upstairs. The gym offers courses for various ages and climbing experience, with highly-motivated trainers and climbers. The boulders are known to be very demanding on endurance, and there are some special circuits set up upstairs. Every autumn they organise a friendly boulder competition.

listings.name: Theater in der Josefstadt
listings.content: Opened in 1776, this is the oldest continually-operating theater in Vienna. At its reopening following a remodeling in 1822 Beethoven directed his commissioned piece Die Weihe des Hauses (The Consecration of the House). Since 1858, it has focused exclusively on theater, and music is no longer performed here. Famous cast members have included Johann Nestroy, Otto Schenk, and Klaus Maria Brandenauer.

listings.name: Vienna's English Theatre
listings.content: The oldest English-language theatre in continental Europe. Tickets can be purchased online.

listings.name: Tunnel
listings.content: Student's place. Nice breakfast, live music every day starting about 21:00.

listings.name: Puerta del Sol
listings.content: One of the best tapas bars in Vienna. Both the cold and warm tapas are excellent, and one can choose from amongst 90 wines.

listings.name: Curry Insel
listings.content: Sri Lankan restaurant with a good range of vegetarian dishes. Free WiFi.

listings.name: Deli Bluem
listings.content: The vegan restaurant cooks local ingredients.

listings.name: Il Sestante
listings.content: This Italian restaurant serves pizza fired in a stone oven. It has a nice view of the Maria Treu plaza, with outdoor seating in the summer.

listings.name: Konoba
listings.content: The delicious aromas of garlic and grilled fish invite the passerby into this Croatian seafood restaurant.

listings.name: Prinz Ferdinand
listings.content: An Austrian Beisl that serves good food and even some vegetarian options.

listings.name: Schnattl
listings.content: For more than 25 years the restaurant has been serving Viennese and international cuisine of a high standard.

listings.name: Speisekammer
listings.content: A small new fancy underground restaurant, with a rotating roster of young chefs who prepare freely-improvised dishes. A special feature is the surprise menu (Überraschungsmenu), where you can choose the ingredients of your meal, but not the manner of preparation.

listings.name: Cafe der Provinz
listings.content: Cute little coffee place sells mostly organic products. Serves breakfast, gallettes, and crêpes.

listings.name: Café Eiles
listings.content: This café has been operating since 1840, when the building was completed. The interior dates from the last redesign in 1933.

listings.name: Café Florianihof
listings.content: A very popular café that has been redecorated. It serves good food with many vegetarian options for fair prices and typical Austrian desserts like "Topfen-knöderl" or "Powiderl-Tascherl". Free Wi-Fi. Most of the places are non-smoking.

listings.name: Café Merkur
listings.content: On Saturdays and Sundays offers breakfast almost all day. Due to its good prices it is a popular hang-out for students. Has Wi-Fi access.

listings.name: Kaffeemodul
listings.content: A tiny coffee gem in Vienna, easily overlooked by passersby, with very skilled baristas.

listings.name: People on Caffeine
listings.content: Hidden away in a former Catholic sacristy, this café offers fair trade and special roasted coffee. Serves espresso and many of the newer filtered coffee styles.

listings.name: Gürtel
listings.content: Many bars and music-oriented venues are under the elevated subway tracks.

listings.name: B72
listings.content: The bar also serves as a venue for hip hop and modern music concerts.

listings.name: Chelsea
listings.content: Serving a wide range of international beers, this popular place is often fully-packed.

listings.name: Rhiz
listings.content: Rhiz promotes experimental music for an alternative audience; it's well worth checking out the online program of upcoming concerts. This bar tends to be particularly smoky.

listings.name: Hotel Graf Stadion
listings.content: The house was built in the Biedermeier Epoche style in 1824/1825 and is registered as a historic monument; it has been run as a hotel since 1897. 39 singles and doubles with bath with shower/WC, hair dryer, clothesline, SAT-Flatscreen-TV, radio, telephone and free WLAN in the entire hotel.

listings.name: Mercure Josefshof Vienna
listings.content: The hotel is located on a quiet side street. It provides free Wi-Fi and has a small basement garage for cars.

listings.name: The Levante Laudon
listings.content: Rents apartments on a quiet street behind the city hall (Rathaus). All apartments have a usable small kitchen; the two-room apartments have separated living rooms and bedrooms. Perfectly suitable for families.

listings.name: Hotel Zipser
listings.content: The Jugendstil hotel in the centre of Vienna is a family-run business, and offers special rates for families.

listings.name: The Levante Parliament
listings.content: The centrally-located boutique hotel has a beautiful atrium and the Nemtoi Restaurant-Bar. Has free Wi-Fi, as well as fitness and spa rooms.

listings.name: Schloß Belvedere
listings.content: Intended as a summer residence for Prince Eugene of Savoy, was outside the city walls. Its two palace segments, the Upper and Lower Belvedere, later became the permanent home of the Austrian Gallery.
listings.price: Combination ticket for Upper and Lower Palaces: €19 (adults), €15.50 (seniors/students), free (under 18)

listings.name: Österreichische Galerie Belvedere
listings.content: Contains recent Austrian and international art from the past two centuries. Viennese art from the early 20th century is well-represented in the permanent collection Vienna around 1900 and the Art of the Classical Modern, and includes masterpieces from Gustav Klimt, Oskar Kokoschka, and Egon Schiele, as well as earlier works by the Biedermeier painter Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller.

listings.name: Unteres Belvedere
listings.content: The Lower Belvedere and Orangery house temporary exhibits. The Baroque state rooms including the Marble Gallery, Golden Room, and Grotesque Hall are open for normal visiting.

listings.name: Prunkstall
listings.content: The former stables now house a permanent collection of medieval religious art and a collection of medieval tapestries.

listings.name: 21er Haus
listings.content: Has a permanent exhibit of works by the Austrian sculptor/architect Fritz Wotruba, and hosts rotating exhibits of international contemporary art.

listings.name: KunstHausWien
listings.content: Even an avowed hater of modern art can appreciate this. This is Hundertwasser's (born Friedrich Stowasser in 1928) major contribution to the Viennese art world. In a time when artists often try to shock the public or merely impress other members of the rarefied gallery subculture, Hundertwasser's KunstHausWien would be a bastion against the dictatorship of the straight line, the ruler and T-square, a bridgehead against the grid system and the chaos of the absurd. Starting with the façade of the building, adapted from its prior life as a furniture factory, there is a Gaudi-in-Barcelona feel to the place. Windows peek out like eyes from curvy, rounded plaster and colorful paint. It is a Disneyland for grownups.

listings.name: Heeresgeschichtliches Museum
listings.content: A huge museum featuring weapons and military maps from different periods. You can also see the open-top car in which Archduke Franz Ferdinand, the last Austrian prince, was shot in Sarajevo. His death triggered World War I and the eventual downfall of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. In the same room as this is the visibly blood-stained jacket he was wearing at the time of his assassination.

listings.name: Fälschermuseum
listings.content: Unique museum devoted to art forgery. Houses a large collection of counterfeited paintings, many from highly-skilled, infamous forgers. Includes several pages of the infamous fake Hitler diaries which fooled numerous experts in the early 1980s.

listings.name: Remise - Verkehrsmuseum der Wiener Linien
listings.content: This museum in a former depot houses a comprehensive collection of vintage vehicles explaining the history of Viennese public transport. The exhibits include horse-drawn streetcars from 1868, a steam tram set from 1885, many electric streetcars from the 1910s until the recent past, and buses from 1949-1978, including the infamous "Reichsbrücken-Bus" which fell into the Danube but was recovered and repaired to run for many more years. The simulator of a U-Bahn train is considered the highlight among guests. Attached small gift shop. Major labels are in English and German, but some smaller items are labelled in German only.

listings.name: Hundertwasserhaus
listings.content: Interesting apartment/office complex, designed by the Austrian architect/painter Hundertwasser. Remember that most of it is still in use as housing or offices and respect the residents' privacy. The nearby KunstHausWien (see above) is a Hundertwasser building you can freely explore.

listings.name: Schwarzenbergplatz
listings.content: The Schwarzenberg place is a big square in inner Vienna. It is faced by many palaces amongst them the Palais Schwarzenberg, the hosue of industry, the French embassy and others.The square runs next to the RIng.

listings.name: Heldendenkmal der Roten Armee
listings.content: An imposing Soviet-style monument near Karlsplatz commemorates the Soviet victory in Vienna over the Nazi army.

listings.name: Arnold Schönberg Center
listings.content: This building houses an archive of the works of the Viennese composer, with a permanent exhibit relating to his work and music and a gallery of his paintings.
listings.price: €5 (adults), €3 (seniors/students), free (children under 12), 10% reduction for Vienna Card

listings.name: Sankt Marxer Friedhof
listings.content: This historic cemetery was in use from 1784 until 1874. Mozart was buried here in an unmarked pauper's grave in 1791; the tombstone dates from a later period, after his grave was tentatively identified. The Bezirksmuseum Landstraße offers regular guided tours of the cemetery (in German).

listings.name: Botanischer Garten
listings.content: Established in 1754 by Empress Maria Theresia as a garden for medicinal plants and granted to the University of Vienna, which has maintained it since. The gardens contain a number of rare plants, including alpine specimens.

listings.name: Konzerthaus
listings.content: Built between 1911 and 1913, the Konzerthaus is the homebase for the Vienna Symphony (Wiener Symphoniker), the Vienna Chamber Orchestra (Wiener Kammerorchester), the Wiener Singakademie and the Klangforum Wien.

listings.name: Arena
listings.content: The arena is one of the biggest concert and alternative culture places. The slaughterhouse got squatted in 1976 and operates since as culture center. FM4 hosts here its annual birthday party. The programme lists the performing artists. The open air arena can host 3000 peoples.

listings.name: Akademietheater
listings.content: The Akademietheater is the smaller of two performance halls of the Burgtheater ensemble. It was built between 1911 and 1913 by the architects Fellner und Hellmer and Ludwig Baumann.

listings.name: Ice skating
listings.content: At the Wiener Eislaufverein in winter time one can skate on a big 6000 m² square.

listings.name: Vegetasia
listings.content: Chain of vegetarian restaurants. Serves a huge variety of Taiwanese Buddhist vegetarian food. Most of it vegan, many meat imitations. Non-smoking.

listings.name: Rochusmarkt
listings.content: Typical Viennese outdoor market with fresh produce as well as stalls selling baked goods and other prepared food.

listings.name: Amon
listings.content: The restaurant serves seasonal Viennese food typically of course plates with large quantities. The cellar is a vinothek with a good selection of Austrian wines.

listings.name: Benkei
listings.content: Favorite place from nearby Japanese embassy. The place has a bit dated interior.

listings.name: El Fontroussi
listings.content: The Belgium restaurant in this renovated tavern offers seafood with refined sauces. Daily lunch menu.

listings.name: Marx Restauration
listings.content: The restaurant inside an old butchery serves modern Viennese food. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: No. 27
listings.content: The Chinese restaurant is best visited with several persons to be able to taste their different plates.

listings.name: O'Connor's Old Oak
listings.content: Gareth "Gaz" Smith is cooking here daily, hence this Irish pub may serve the best Irish food in Vienna (not only legendary fish and chips).

listings.name: Pho & Saigon Market NR
listings.content: A Vietnamese restaurant next to the shop has small delicate choices. The cellar has one table tennis.

listings.name: Sri Thai Imbiss
listings.content: The small cellar place cooks Thai food (green curry,..) on the spicy side of life.

listings.name: Taverna Lefteris
listings.content: The Cretan (not Greek) restaurant changes its menu daily.

listings.name: Rochus
listings.content: Contemporary Viennese and European cuisine. Vegan options available. Extensive wine and cocktail list.

listings.name: al Italiana
listings.content: Traditional Italian pizzeria and trattoria. Friendly service, extensive menu, good wine list. Popular with locals.

listings.name: Meierei im Stadtpark
listings.content: The very posh restaurant offers 120 different cheese varieties combined with freshly baked Viennese bread. This is the "bistro" of the Steiereck, but still extremely classy.

listings.name: Steirereck im Stadtpark
listings.content: The most renowned Austrian restaurant in middle of the beautiful Stadtpark is defintely worth a visit. Heinz Reitbauer is cooking with exotic or mostly forgotten natural herbs. Much of the menu features modernistic presentations of traditional Central European meats such as venison, carp, and crayfish. Adi Schmid is the leading Sommelier. Reservation in advance is definitely needed.

listings.name: That’s Amore
listings.content: Italian cooks use well chosen products for their pizzas.

listings.name: Cafe Menta
listings.content: Designed by Robin Molenaar and Yvonne Krisch with Rainer seats and an industrial bar, the café has a cool look plus interesting vegetarian options.

listings.name: Intermezzo Bar
listings.content: Incredible lustre above the bar from the 1960s.

listings.name: Salm Bräu
listings.content: The brewery has a Viennese kitchen, but people mostly come for the good beer.

listings.name: Strandbar Hermann
listings.content: The outdoor bar serves daily happy hour cocktails during 18:00-19:00. As the name tells it is a bar on sand next to the Danube canal near the Urania.

listings.name: Vienna Sporthotel
listings.content: Spa and tennis possibilities.

listings.name: Hotel Am Konzerthaus - MGallery Collection
listings.content: The rooms are nice and smallish, but still stylish.

listings.name: Best Western Plus Amedia Hotel Wien
listings.content: Rather boring outside and inside (although with liberal use of red), the hotel is easy to miss at the far end of Landstrasser Hauptstrasse. Amedia marks high on comfort, cleaniness and service, which is a combination rarely found in Viennese hotels.

listings.name: Lindner Hotel Am Belvedere
listings.content: Surprisingly tasteful, with large rooms, oversized beds and very reasonable pricing - and next to the Belvedere gardens indeed. You can get airline miles with many frequent flier programmes by staying at Lindner hotels.

listings.name: Mercure Grand Hotel Biedermeier Wien
listings.content: More Biedermeier than grand, this Mercure is a very typical representative of Viennese hotels, with questionable colours and patterns, all wrapped in a vaguely historic setting. That said, the unusually large rooms (esp. Privilege) make it an option worth considering. Many rooms face the narrow internal courtyard, i.e. another room's windows within a short distance.

listings.name: NH Wien Belvedere
listings.content: The NH corporate unformization did not quite make it to this hotel, but you can expect reasonable standards - and a simpler format of the typical Viennese hotel. Next door to the Lindner, the NH is indeed close to the Belvedere

listings.name: Austria Trend Hotel Savoyen
listings.content: The hotel offers spacious and modern rooms including great breakfast.

listings.name: Hilton Vienna
listings.content: Home to Vienna’s premier conference centre. Features meeting space for 2-1,800 and provides a business service centre.

listings.name: Imperial Riding School Renaissance Vienna
listings.content: This Renaissance is one of the Marriott properties scattered across Vienna, located in a renovated historic building of the former Imperial Riding School - not to be confused with the Spanish Riding School, which is far away from it. With an impressive interior and rooms appointed with decorations referencing the equine history, it surely does impress.

listings.name: Intercontinental Wien
listings.content: See above for the bar.

listings.name: Spiess & Spiess
listings.content: Classy older hotel on a quiet side street, tastefully renovated and modernized. Good-quality breakfast buffet included in the price.

listings.name: Margareten Platz
listings.content: The biggest older square in Margareten.

listings.name: Margareten-Hof
listings.content: Built by the architects Ferdinand Fellner und Hermann Helmer in 1884/85.

listings.name: Margaretenbrunnen
listings.content: It was built to thank for the access to the fresh water pipeline going to the central imperial palace for Margareten in 1835/36. It features Saint Margarete killing a dragon.

listings.name: Matzleinsdorfer Pfarrkirche
listings.content: Two previous churches were located here, the most recent a Baroque building from the 18th century, which despite massive popular protest was demolished in 1965 due to traffic considerations. The new steel and concrete church was designed by the German architect Rudolf Schwarz and built between 1961-1965. A defining characteristic is the interplay of light concrete and dark glass, with the entry side featuring an oversized cross motif, and the side featuring a herringbone pattern. The main altar from the old church, painted by F.X. Wagenschön and depicting the transfiguration of St Florian, is now located in the organ loft of the new church.

listings.name: The "Red Vienna": Community Housing of the 1920s and 1930s
listings.content: During a short period from 1919 to 1933, the city of Vienna erected some 65,000 apartments of high quality for the impoverished working class. Highly noticeable is also the contemporary architecture of these buildings all across town, of which several interesting ones are clustered on a short stretch along Gürtel road. The style ranges from Art Déco to modernistic, the buildings have courtyards and often resemble fortresses – as which they were even used during the civil war 1934. Look out for the 1920s , type=see name=Metzleinsthaler Hof lat=48.18146 long=16.34872 image=Metzleinstaler Hof 1.JPG, type=see name=Matteottihof lat=48.18190 long=16.35062 image=Matteottihof.JPG, or the 1950s high rise building of Matzleinsdorf just nearby. Show respect while visiting, as these are living houses and not tourist attractions in the first place.

listings.name: Filmcasino
listings.content: This very stylish cinema screens carefully chosen films.

listings.name: On
listings.content: A Chinese/Asian restaurant that gets consistent excellent gourmet reviews.

listings.name: Rudi's Beisl
listings.content: This Austrian Beisl likes to put "Panier" on everything.

listings.name: Silberwirt
listings.content: The "Beisl" is very popular amongst local Viennese.

listings.name: Waldviertler Hof
listings.content: This traditional Vienna restaurant offers good seasonal food and beer choices. The restaurant is non-smoking. Each room is specifically decorated, one of them is a traditional Zirben-Stube. The prices are fair and the portions big.

listings.name: Weinschenke Franzensgasse
listings.content: Chef Nikolai Kölbl serves enchanting versions of Viennese food. There are vegetarian options and the salads are good.

listings.name: Woracziczky
listings.content: A modern interpretation of traditional Viennese food like Tafelspitzsulz, Blunzentascherln, Zwiebelrostbraten, and Kalbsrahmgulasch. It is particularly popular for its casual atmosphere and tasty, delicate food.

listings.name: Zum Schwarzen Adler
listings.content: The "Gasthaus" serves Viennese food and Hackl Bräu (workers' beer).

listings.name: propeller
listings.content: Cozy breakfast/lunch cafe with popular cocktails at night

listings.name: Senhor Vinho
listings.content: The Portuguese restaurant offers Bacalhao, Pastel de Nata and many different Portuguese wines.

listings.name: Café Cuadro
listings.content: The café serves breakfast, later cocktails and burgers, beware that people are heavily smoking.

listings.name: Café Rüdigerhof
listings.content: The Rüdigerhof is a typical Viennese café, hence expect rude waiters (treat them with humor) and have enough time to chill out. It offers nice seats outdoor under trees next to the Vienna river. Indoor can be very smoky.

listings.name: Motto
listings.content: It is a bar, a restaurant, a gallery and a concert location. The bar serves good wines and cocktails. It is a location for smokers.

listings.name: Pub Klemo
listings.content: The wine bar and shop has an incredible choice over 3000 different wines.

listings.name: Reinprechtsstüberl
listings.content: It serves upper Austrian monastery beer Schlägl and must ("Most").

listings.name: Transporter Bar
listings.content: The popular minimalistic bar with fair trade juices, long drinks features life DJ acts. It has free Wi-Fi access. The table-tennis table is used every Wednesday for a ping-pong evening.

listings.name: WerkzeugH
listings.content: The young architect Manfred Wuits together with the cook Zeljko Jovanovic transformed the previous tool hall/shop to an innovative popular bohemian bar. In summer time one can sit outside. There is free Wi-Fi. Usually on Sundays they organise special breakfast.

listings.name: Hotel Allegro
listings.content: Rough location on the corner of busy streets incluting Gürtel it is hence easy accessible and has fast connections.

listings.name: The Art hotel Vienna
listings.content: a modern 3-star hotel

listings.name: Falkensteiner Hotel Wien Margareten
listings.content: Opened in 2013 it is designed by architect Matteo Thun. It offers free Wi-Fi, a sauna, and a steam bath.

listings.name: Pentahotel Vienna
listings.content: The hotel has a café bar and stylish rooms designed by Matteo Thun.
